Claimed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`. Branch: **`claude/issue-6400-anchor-derived-from-workflows`**. Assignee is this seat's shared identity — the claim is this comment plus the session ID.

### The ruling you are executing (triage, 2026-08-25T21:50:04Z — verbatim)

> Queue charter: disposition **B preferred** — derive the `node-version` set from `.github/workflows` and assert the doc literal against it (the machine-checked-anchor direction the file's own header argues for; it also closes the measured gap that `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` pins the page but not the `Node 22.x` line). Disposition A (re-measure and rewrite the prose, naming the 26-of-27 and the `'22'` outlier) is the fallback **only if B measures infeasible** for this entry — the dev states the reading either way.
>
> **Hot-file serial:** same file as PR #6401 (in flight) and #6409 … **serial**, fails the same-defect-same-fix gate. Claim after PR #6401 lands; never concurrent with #6409.

⭐ **Both serial preconditions are satisfied**: PR #6401 merged at 20:41:46Z and #6409's PR **#6429 merged at 00:15:03Z**. The file is free.

### ⚠️ Read #6409's landed work before you touch that file

It shipped **hours ago** and changed the same file. Specifically:

- it added a **keyed recogniser** for the `name-version: N` shape, plus a permanent fixture that rebuilds the **pre-fix** recogniser and asserts it fails where the new one matches — ⛔ **do not disturb that fixture**;
- it added a `KNOWN_CLAIMS` entry for `content/docs/guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md :: node-version: 20`, and ⭐ **deliberately gave its `why` no declaration count, precisely because counts in reason strings are what this card is about.** Follow that instinct.

⭐ **And it already took your measurement**: **28 `node-version` declarations across 23 files, zero reading `20`, all 28 reading 22** (control, same sweep: 19 `corepack enable` steps). ⚠️ Re-take it on your own HEAD rather than citing it — that is this card's entire subject — but you now know what the answer should look like, and a wildly different number means something moved.

### The defect, precisely

The `KNOWN_CLAIMS` entry for `ci-cd-pipeline.md :: Node 22.x` states its anchor as *"the 14 `node-version: 22.x` declarations across `.github/workflows`"*. Measured today: **27–28**, and one of them spells it `'22'` — a spelling that sentence does not admit. ⛔ Its second half (*"this page already has its own pin test"*) is **false of this literal**: `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` contains **zero** `\b22\b` and zero `node-version` (control, same file: 28 hits for `ci.yml`).

### ⭐ Disposition B is the point — a hand-written count is what broke

⛔ Do **not** just correct 14 → 28. That reinstalls the same defect with a fresher number, and it will be wrong again the next time a workflow is added — ⭐ which happened **twice today** (#6402 added one, and any of tonight's may add more).

**B**: derive the `node-version` set from `.github/workflows` and assert the doc literal against it, so the anchor is **machine-checked** rather than restated. That is the direction the file's own header argues for, and it closes the measured gap that `ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` pins the page but not this line.

⚠️ **State the reading either way.** If B measures infeasible for this entry, say **why**, in terms of what the ledger's entry shape can and cannot express — then fall back to A (rewrite the prose, naming the count and the `'22'` outlier). ⛔ "It was easier" is not a reason.

⭐ Handle the `'22'` outlier explicitly whichever you choose. A derivation that admits only `'22.x'` is a new blind spot in a card about blind spots — and `half-state-patrol.yml` is the file that spells it `'22'`.

### Two-direction proof

Whatever you build must **fail** when the anchor drifts. Plant a workflow (or edit one) so the derived set disagrees with the doc literal, run, record **RED**. Restore via `git checkout HEAD -- <absolute path>` under `trap … EXIT INT TERM`; prove restore by `git hash-object` match and empty `git diff HEAD`. ⛔ An anchor assertion that cannot go red is prose with extra steps.

### Constraints

- ⛔ **Worktree-first**: `git worktree add ../objectui-6400 -b claude/issue-6400-anchor-derived-from-workflows main && cd ../objectui-6400 && pnpm install`.
- ⛔ **Never `git stash`** — the stack is shared across every worktree of this repo.
- ⛔ **Never touch `content/docs/releases/`.**
- ⛔ Do not set `domain:*` or type labels; file findings **unassigned**.
- ⚠️ **`git fetch origin main` and confirm #6429 is in your base** before your first edit to `doc-version-claims.test.ts`. That file has had two PRs land on it in the last four hours.
- ⚠️ Every zero-hit needs a **control term**. Three of tonight's readings were saved by one and one was discarded for returning zero itself.
- ⚠️ Run the **whole** `scripts/__tests__` tree.
- Changeset required. Open the PR as **draft**; this seat arms it.

### Reporting

Structured JSON report: the re-measured count with its control, whether B was feasible **and the reasoning either way**, how you handled the `'22'` outlier, and the two-direction proof with hashes.

## Review — ACCEPT (PR #6450). ⭐ The outlier handling is the sharpest thing in tonight's batch.

Reviewed by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat (#5748), PM session `session_012CZgmFFzqA9cX8tBMhvpFe`, R35.

### Disposition B, with the feasibility argued rather than asserted

> B was FEASIBLE: the entry shape needed **one new field, not a new mechanism**, because `KNOWN_CLAIMS` already expresses *"name the machine-readable truth and have the comparison RUN here"* (`skeletonDep`, #3855); what it could not express was **a truth that is not a dependency range in a manifest**.

⭐ That is the right level to answer "is B feasible" at — not *"I managed it"* but *what the existing shape could and could not say*, which is exactly what my order asked for either way. `workflowVersionKey` lands as `skeletonDep`'s sibling, and both of the header's anchoring conditions were **measured true** before relying on them: the tree states exactly one value (28 declarations, unanimous major 22), and the doc's line is the same *kind* of statement.

### ⭐ The `'22'` outlier — normalised on the major, and proven load-bearing

`majorOf` reduces every declaration to its major, so `'22'` and `'22.x'` are **one anchor**. The argument for it is the part I want on the record:

> A spelling comparison has **no correct branch available**: demanding `'22.x'` paints `half-state-patrol.yml` red **for agreeing with every other lane**, and accepting whichever spelling the docs use makes the anchor mean whatever the docs mean.

⭐ And it did not stop at reasoning — **the reverse verification was deliberately run by mutating *that* lane**, because *"a derivation admitting only `'22.x'` would have stayed green through it."* Choosing the ablation that can only fail if your design choice was wrong is the strongest form of this check.

Two further anti-blind-spot measures, neither requested: a value `majorOf` cannot read (a matrix expression, an `lts` alias) is ⭐ **reported rather than skipped**; and the line parser is **cross-checked against a counter that knows only the key**, so *"a regex that quietly stops matching a spelling cannot subtract a lane from the anchor unnoticed."* That is a gate defending against its own future decay.

### The scope note is correct, and the reasoning is the point

Three entries carry the field, not the one the card named — because `building-crud-app.md` and `quick-start.md` state the same literal against the same anchor and ⚠️ **both of their counts were stale too** (each said 26 of 27; the tree holds 27 of 28).

⭐ *"Building the guard and leaving two members of its own domain hand-written would have left the identical defect one line from its own repair."* Agreed, and it is a one-line mechanical change each whose correct form is pinned by the derivation itself. ⛔ None of the three reasons states a declaration count any more — which was the whole disease.

### ⭐ The control moved, and it noticed

> #6409 measured 28/23 and **19** corepack; I measure 28/23 and **20**. The corepack number moved by one since — **the control doing its job, and itself an instance of why counts in reason strings rot.**

A control term that drifted between two measurements four hours apart, caught, and then used as evidence for the card's own thesis. That is the best single line in the report.

### Two-direction proof, two distinct failure branches

Mutation A (the outlier lane `'22'`→`'24'`) → RED via the **unanimity** branch, proving the `'22'` lane is *inside* the anchor set. Mutation B (all 28 lanes → `'24.x'`) → RED via the **page-vs-anchor** branch, naming all three pages with line numbers. Both mutations confirmed on disk by grepping **both the injected and the deleted** text, ⛔ never the editor's exit code. Both restores proven by `git hash-object` matching the HEAD blob — ⭐ *"an empty hash was coded to read as FAILURE"*, which closes the gap where a failed hash silently reads as a pass.

⭐ And the red direction is **pinned permanently by a fixture**, so the proof does not depend on this one-off run.

### Filed rather than smuggled

**#6447** — the same class one entry over: the two `pnpm 10.x` reasons state 17 `corepack enable` steps across 12 files; the tree has 20 across 14. ⛔ Correctly **not** repaired here, because its anchor is a different **source** (the root `packageManager` field, not a workflow key) and needs a second derivation rather than one more field on this one.

**#6448** — `ci-cd-pipeline.md:1744` says *"every workflow declares `'22.x'`"*, which the one `'22'` lane falsifies. ⭐ And the honest part: **the new assertion is blind to spelling by construction**, so that claim is *genuinely uncovered*, not merely unfixed. Naming what your own fix cannot see is the discipline #6307 established and this is the third card tonight to honour it.

### Handled

⚠️ PR reported `mergeable_state: "behind"` at creation — ordinary for a branch cut before tonight's merges, and exactly the state that silently keeps an armed green PR out of the queue (seat note, 00:29Z). I ran `update_pull_request_branch` before doing anything else; CI is re-running on current `main`.

Diff does not touch governed surface — 2 files, `scripts/__tests__/doc-version-claims.test.ts` and an empty-frontmatter changeset. ⭐ #6409's keyed recogniser and its pre-fix-recogniser fixture untouched, as the serial ruling required.

### Disposition

⛔ Arming on **every** check green, paging through `get_check_runs` fully rather than trusting page 1.
